title: Papadimitriou–Yannakakis NP-completeness Conjecture
statement_text: The Exact Matching problem (EM) is NP-complete.
context_text: Papadimitriou and Yannakakis introduced EM in 1982 while studying restricted minimum weight spanning tree problems, and conjectured it to be NP-complete. This was later cast into doubt when Mulmuley, Vazirani and Vazirani showed EM $\in$ RP, making NP-hardness unlikely under standard complexity assumptions.
paper_contribution: Proves EM is solvable in deterministic polynomial time for graphs of independence number at most $\alpha$ (running time $n^{O(2^{O(\alpha)})}$) and for bipartite graphs of bipartite independence number at most $\beta$, providing new infinite families of graph classes for which EM is in P.
paper_title: Exact Matching in Graphs of Bounded Independence Number

title: Conjecture 3
statement_text: The problem of counting perfect matchings in input graphs of independence number $2$ is $\#P$-complete.
context_text: The independence number of a graph is the maximum size of an independent set; graphs of independence number $2$ include all complements of triangle-free graphs. In the Exact Matching problem (EM), introduced by Papadimitriou and Yannakakis, one is given a graph whose edges are coloured red or blue and an integer $k$, and asks whether there is a perfect matching with exactly $k$ red edges; it is in RP (Mulmuley, Vazirani and Vazirani) but no deterministic polynomial algorithm is known in general. The authors give deterministic algorithms for EM running in time $n^{2^{O(\alpha)}}$ on graphs of independence number $\alpha$ (and similarly for bipartite graphs of bounded bipartite independence number). They note that for all graph classes on which EM was previously known to be polynomial (planar graphs, $K_{3,3}$-minor-free graphs, graphs of bounded genus, complete and complete bipartite graphs) perfect matchings can also be counted in polynomial time; in contrast, they are not aware of polynomial counting schemes even for graphs of independence number $2$, and conjecture that counting is hard there. In the conclusion they ask to prove this conjecture, or to find deterministic polynomial-time algorithms for EM on classes where counting perfect matchings is #P-hard.
